title: Study problem: presidential cost priorities and bilingual-education duties
shortTitle: Study problem: presidential cost priorities and bilingual-education duties
summary: Test the difference between directing a lawful choice and replacing the criterion Congress required.
notes:
The classroom hypothetical asks what follows if a bilingual-education statute directs an agency to select the educationally most effective program regardless of expense, while the President directs use of the most cost-effective program regardless of educational efficacy. Start with the enacted criterion and identify the factual or policy discretion it leaves. A supervisory instruction that selects within that discretion differs from an instruction that changes the controlling criterion.

Marbury and Kendall support enforcing a lawful mandatory duty; they do not eliminate the need to identify which choices the statute actually settles. Wirt and Taney expose the further institutional question of who may direct discretion assigned to a subordinate. Sierra Club and the OLC regulatory-review memorandum add the possibility of presidential advice or coordination while preserving the officer’s duty to meet the statute. This is an editorial problem with an explanatory analytical path, not a reported judicial judgment.
